suggestions.rationale: Mapping Expansion Batch ME-13 adds this draft-primary relationship only as a bounded clinical proposition. A systematic review and meta-analysis identifies fecal incontinence as an etiologic risk factor for incontinence-associated dermatitis; the approved mapping is restricted to moisture-associated skin damage in the exposed distribution. Require fecal incontinence with repeated or prolonged perineal skin exposure and separately diagnosed moisture-associated or incontinence-associated dermatitis in the exposed distribution. Do not generalize this relationship to eczema, fungal disease, allergic or irritant dermatitis from unrelated agents, pressure injury, cellulitis, or a nonspecific rash. Preserve those alternative skin diagnoses and other causes as competing explanations. The cited literature supports only this constrained proposition and does not, by itself, establish an individual medical nexus.
